Additionally, ground and neutral can only be bonded at the main panel with the main ground - you can't have ground and neutral connected at any sub-panel, outlet, or receptacle.

If you have 12/2wg out to the j-box in the shop, then you can only have either 120 or 240 volt service, not both (the uninsulated conductor must be grounded, the white-insulated conductor in the cable could carry either neutral or the other hot, but if it carries the other hot then it should be marked with red or black vinyl tape at both ends). This configuration with 12/2wg carrying 240 volts is very common for outlets that serve point-use hot water heaters, small air conditioners, pumps, etc. However, don't underestimate the conductivity of even a long run of copper - the path of least resistance (assuming the one conductor you have isn't broken) is definitely going to be back to the panel over the ground. That said, make sure you use outdoor-rated junction boxes (the new in-use covers are great, if your plug fits under them) and GFCI receptacles and/or breakers to make sure that both the neutral and ground are always properly connected (which will probably mean re-running wire).
